Robota-Embed: Unified VLA Embeddings for Robot
In-Context Learning and Evolution

Yunze Liu1,*,  Jing Wang1,*,  Shenrui Wu3,  Wenkun He2,  Guanqi Zhan1, Xianzheng Ma4,  Junyu Chen1,  Wenhang Ge1,  Haozhan Tang5,  Yuchao Gu1, Zhuoyang Zhang2,  Zekai Wang3,  Dantong Niu3,  Zhen Dong1,  Yuke Zhu1, Trevor Darrell3,  Linxi “Jim” Fan1,  Song Han2,  Han Cai1,†\dagger 1 NVIDIA 2 MIT 3 UCB 4 Oxford 5 CMU
* Equal contribution. †\dagger Corresponding author. Project Page
Abstract

Retrieving useful context for a robot requires matching not only its task, but also its current stage of execution and the continuation that should follow. We introduce Robota-Embed, to our knowledge the first vision–language–action (VLA) embedding model to jointly encode all three modalities in both current-state queries and recorded future continuations. Predictive retrieval training aligns these endpoints for physical-experience retrieval, and the resulting representation retrieves historical continuations as context at inference time. We construct a multi-source corpus of 1,695,684 cleaned training anchors and introduce Robota-Embed-Bench, which evaluates 4,000 queries against a shared 8,000-entry gallery. Our model achieves 47.33% clip-level and 81.77% episode-level R@1, surpassing action-free Gemini Embedding 2 by 22.09 and 33.47 percentage points. Across controlled retrieval studies, removing native action degrades retrieval more than removing vision, indicating that execution information is a central part of the retrieval key. We then study how this shared retrieval space transfers beyond retrieval metrics through two complementary applications. Embed2ICL uses retrieved experience for training-free and training-based policy conditioning, increasing success from 47.0% to 56.3% in DROID-Sim and from 86.4% to 92.8% on the LIBERO difficult subset. Both interfaces also improve task progress in real-robot evaluations. Embed2Evolve uses execution feedback to grow task-local memory and refine how retrieved context is used around a frozen GPT-6 Astra policy. Across five ManiSkill tasks, it achieves 68% success, compared with 24% for GPT-6 Astra Direct and 33% for a harness independently evolved with Omni-Embed-Nemotron-3B under the same protocol. Relative to the latter, it uses approximately 79.5% fewer policy tokens per test rollout. Together, these results show that a unified, action-aware retrieval space can support both robot in-context learning and task-local context evolution.
